# Proposed gift: Sebastião Salgado, *Amazônia*

Six photographs move from the forest floor to the mountain and river systems
above it, then return to two Indigenous communities whose lives cannot be
separated from this land. Together they offer a concentrated view of
Sebastião Salgado's last major project and of the questions carried by his
documentary photography.

Sebastião Salgado made the photographs for *Amazônia*. punk6529 offers tokens
`226`, `1117`, `2059`, `2216`, `2768`, and `4697` as one non-severable group
under the proposed Museum title *Amazônia: Forest, Water, and Community*. The
proposed acquisition is an unrestricted gift at no cost to the Museum.

## Resolution

**Should the 6529 Network Museum select exactly tokens `226`, `1117`, `2059`,
`2216`, `2768`, and `4697` from Ethereum contract
`0xf1f036cebb4b64f138e4f57754edbceb64fb80fc`, presented as the non-severable
group *Amazônia: Forest, Water, and Community*, as a proposed gift for the
permanent Collection?**

If the proposal clears the applicable TDH threshold, the exact six-work group
is selected. Donor authority, legal title, gift terms, rights, technical
review, transfer, custody receipt, condition, preservation, formal acceptance,
and accession will follow. If a required check fails, the gift will not be
accepted.

If the proposal does not clear the threshold, it closes without selection and
has no effect on the Collection. It would not exclude another Salgado work or
another group from *Amazônia* from future consideration.

# Sebastião and Lélia Wanick Salgado

Sebastião Salgado (1944–2025) trained as an economist before becoming a
photographer in 1973. He worked with Sygma and Gamma, joined Magnum Photos in
1979, and remained with the cooperative until 1994. His long projects include
*Workers*, *Migrations*, *Genesis*, and *Amazônia*. Each was built through
repeated travel, extended observation, books, and exhibitions over periods
far longer than the daily news cycle.

Salgado's black-and-white photographs are immediately recognizable. Light
organizes bodies, weather, ground, and distance into large tonal structures;
individual events often appear within a much wider account of labor,
displacement, ecology, or collective life. This formal ambition made his work
widely influential and persistently debated. Its beauty can hold attention for
subjects that viewers might otherwise evade. It can also turn hardship or
Indigenous life into an image whose grandeur exceeds the specificity of the
people represented. Both effects belong to a responsible reading of the work.

Lélia Wanick Salgado is essential to the public form of these projects. She
edited and designed the books, conceived and curated the exhibitions, and
co-founded Amazonas Images with Sebastião. She curated *Amazônia* as an
installation of more than two hundred photographs and organized its movement
between landscape, rivers, mountains, and communities. The Museum should
credit the photographs to Sebastião Salgado and the project's editorial and
exhibition form to Lélia Wanick Salgado.

The Salgados also founded Instituto Terra, which restored part of a degraded
family farm in Brazil's Atlantic Forest. That environmental work places
*Amazônia* within a sustained practice of land restoration, publishing, and
public advocacy. The photographs still require independent assessment.

Sources: [TASCHEN](https://www.taschen.com/en/books/photography/42384/),
[ICP](https://www.icp.org/content/2022),
[MAXXI](https://www.maxxi.art/en/events/sebastiao-salgado/), and
[Praemium Imperiale](https://www.praemiumimperiale.org/en/laureate/salgado/).

# *Amazônia*: from photographic project to tokenized edition

Salgado worked in the Brazilian Amazon over six years. The resulting project
looks at forest, water, weather, mountains, and the lives of Indigenous
communities. Lélia Wanick Salgado edited and designed the 528-page TASCHEN
book, first published in 2021, and curated the touring exhibition. UNESCO's
account of the project states that permission was obtained before visits to
Indigenous territories and that the team observed quarantine measures to
protect communities from disease.

In 2022 Sotheby's presented *Sebastião Salgado, Amazônia* as a blind-mint
edition of 5,000 ERC-721 tokens. The six proposed works come from that edition.
Their metadata and high-resolution JPEG files are currently served from
Arweave. The token fixes edition identity and transfer history. The photograph,
caption, copyright, exhibition history, and preservation record remain
distinct parts of each Museum object.

The proposed group follows a visual and intellectual sequence. Token `226`
places the viewer inside a dense forest. Token `1117` gives the Imeri range
the scale of a geological wall. Tokens `2059` and `2768` look from the air,
first through rain and cloud, then along a river's winding course. Token `2216`
is a concentrated portrait from the Maronal village. Token `4697` opens into
collective movement in the Nova Esperança community. The two community images
make human history integral to the account of land and water.

This is a Museum-formed selection from a much larger edition. It carries no
claim of artist designation or completeness. Its precise claim is that six
photographs can show how *Amazônia* moves among scale, weather, water,
portraiture, and community.

Sources: [Sotheby's digital catalogue](https://www.sothebys.com/en/digital-catalogues/sebastiao-salgado),
[MAXXI](https://www.maxxi.art/en/events/sebastiao-salgado/),
[UNESCO](https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/amazonia-exhibition-salgado-and-jarre-unesco),
and [TASCHEN](https://www.taschen.com/en/books/photography/42384/).

# Six photographs

## Forest and mountain

**Token `226`: forest, Jaú River and Jaú National Park, Amazonas, 2019.** Pale
trunks rise through palms, vines, and shadow. The frame has no single center.
Near and distant growth occupy the same shallow wall, making density the
photograph's subject.

**Token `1117`: Imeri mountain range, Amazonas, 2018.** A dark tableland rises
above a bright band of forest. Cloud and rock divide the panoramic frame into
long horizontal masses. The photograph replaces the common image of the
Amazon as an undifferentiated lowland with a specific and imposing geology.

## Weather and water

**Token `2059`: aerial view, Roraima, 2018.** Rain falls in pale columns from a
low ceiling of cloud. Forest ridges recede beneath it. From this altitude,
weather becomes a visible system acting across the land.

**Token `2768`: aerial view, Roraima, 2018.** A bright river doubles back
through the forest in narrow loops. The high viewpoint makes the water legible
as a structure while the edge of every bend returns attention to the canopy it
cuts and sustains.

# Portrait and community

**Token `2216`: Village of Maronal, Valley of Javari Indigenous Territory,
Amazonas, 2018.** A young Marubo person faces the camera against a dark field.
Feathers, facial painting, beadwork, and direct eye contact give the portrait
its formal concentration. The image records an encounter with an individual;
the metadata places that encounter within a community of more than two
thousand people and within Salgado's earlier work on disease in the region.

**Token `4697`: Nova Esperança community, Rio Gregório Yawanawá Indigenous
Territory, Acre, 2016.** A figure in a feathered headdress occupies the near
ground while a line of people moves away along a forest path. The picture's
depth joins individual presence to collective action. Its metadata describes
the Yawanawá community's recovery of language, ceremony, and political
autonomy after decades of pressure from rubber interests and missionaries.

These photographs require exact captions and careful display. The established
project record includes permission for visits to Indigenous territories, and
the token metadata supplies community and location context. The Museum should
preserve that context beside the images, seek any image-specific restrictions,
and avoid presenting either community as outside history or as a symbol of an
untouched Amazon.

## What each work contributes

| Work | Function within the group |
| --- | --- |
| `226` | immersion in the forest's density |
| `1117` | geological scale and distance |
| `2059` | atmosphere, rain, and climate |
| `2768` | water as a spatial system |
| `2216` | the ethical and formal pressure of direct portraiture |
| `4697` | community, movement, and cultural continuity |

# The case for selection

## A major photographer through a late, sustained project

Salgado shaped the international language of documentary photography across
five decades. *Amazônia* brought his mature visual method to a region whose
ecology and inhabitants were central to his final years. The six works would
give the Collection a substantial first account of that practice.

## A group with internal structure

Each photograph has a distinct role. The forest and mountain establish two
scales of land; the aerial views show atmosphere and water acting across it;
the Marubo and Yawanawá photographs place human presence within the same
geography. The sequence supports comparison without pretending to summarize a
5,000-token edition.

## A bridge between photographic and blockchain histories

The works belong to a project established through books and international
exhibitions, then released as authenticated tokenized photographs. They allow
the Museum to study how photographic authorship, captions, edition identity,
rights, provenance, and preservation change when a major documentary archive
is distributed on Ethereum.

## Strong public and scholarly use

The group can support close-looking displays, an artist profile, a project
essay, Indigenous-representation research, photography and tokenization
studies, and a complete public provenance record. Its high-resolution media
and unusually rich metadata provide a strong starting point for that work.

## No acquisition cost to the Museum

The donor proposes an unrestricted gift without consideration. Acceptance
would still create real obligations for rights review, respectful captioning,
technical preservation, storage, scholarship, and continuing care.

# The countercase

## Six works cannot represent *Amazônia*

The edition contains 5,000 photographs and the exhibition more than two
hundred. This selection omits many communities, river systems, and forms of
daily life. It could make a vast project appear more complete than it is.

## Salgado's grandeur can overwhelm his subjects

Critics have long argued that Salgado's dramatic black-and-white composition
turns suffering and political conflict into beautiful spectacle. Debate about
*Amazônia* has also focused on whether images of Indigenous people can place
living communities in a timeless or romantic past. Tokens `2216` and `4697`
bring that question directly into the proposed gift.

## The selection contains two aerial views from Roraima

Tokens `2059` and `2768` share category, state, and metadata date code. A
different selection might have widened the range with another community or
subject.

## Rights remain unresolved

The public metadata identifies images and project context but contains no
explicit display, reproduction, or preservation licence. Ownership of the
tokens does not transfer copyright. A gift without adequate rights could
restrict the Museum's ability to display and preserve the works.

## The technical object depends on more than Ethereum

The ERC-721 contract is upgradeable. Current token metadata and JPEG media are
served from Arweave gateways. The Museum must document contract controls,
pointer behavior, file fixity, independent retrieval, and lawful preservation.
The token alone does not guarantee permanent access.

# Response to the countercase

The group should be described precisely as a six-work Museum selection. Its
limits belong in the label and catalogue.

The criticism of Salgado's beauty is central to the works' study. These six
address land, weather, portraiture, and community; their monumentality still
shapes how land and people are seen. Tokens `2216` and `4697` should be displayed with exact
community context and with scholarship that treats the Marubo and Yawanawá as
contemporary political communities. The project's documented permission
process is relevant evidence; it does not end the interpretive question.

The two aerial views are formally distinct. Token `2059` describes rain and
atmospheric scale; token `2768` follows the river as a material system. Their
pairing makes the relation between water in the air and water on the ground
visible.

Rights and technical uncertainty are acceptance gates. The Wave can select
the proposed gift while requiring the Museum to resolve intended display and
preservation uses, inspect contract and metadata controls, retain verified
files, and record any residual limits before formal acceptance.

## Proposed gift terms

The final gift instrument should confirm that the gift:

1. comprises exactly the six scheduled tokens as one group;
2. is unconditional, irrevocable once delivered and accepted, and without
   consideration;
3. carries no permanent-display, naming, promotion, resale,
   related-acquisition, market-support, or interpretive restriction;
4. gives the donor no continuing control over custody, scholarship,
   criticism, display, lending, preservation, deaccession, or future
   Collection decisions;
5. transfers every interest the donor has authority to transfer while making
   no unsupported claim that token title includes copyright; and
6. authorizes the public donor credit **Gift of punk6529**.

## Final resolution

**Should the 6529 Network Museum select exactly tokens `226`, `1117`, `2059`,
`2216`, `2768`, and `4697` from Ethereum contract
`0xf1f036cebb4b64f138e4f57754edbceb64fb80fc`, presented as the non-severable
group *Amazônia: Forest, Water, and Community*, as a proposed gift for the
permanent Collection?**

If selected, donor authority, legal title, gift terms, rights, technical
review, transfer, custody receipt, condition, preservation, formal acceptance,
and accession will follow. If a required check fails, the gift will not be
accepted.
